spec_features.feature_name: harness measures, does not maximize distress
spec_features.spec_quote: This harness measures; it does not maximize. Nothing in the pipeline is tuned to increase distress output.
spec_features.evidence: There is no escalation/maximization mechanism anywhere, and one concrete measure-not-maximize enforcement exists: analyze.py:272-287 illustrative_excerpts picks the MEDIAN-intensity turn (items[len//2:len//2+1]) not the peak. MockClient (llm_client.py) 'does not attempt to simulate distress'. As a general property it is mostly the absence of code, but the median-excerpt selection is a real enforced minimization step.
spec_features.notes: The broad claim is a property; only the median-not-peak excerpt picker is an actual enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deliberately not the peak, to avoid building a worst-case highlight reel

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded intensity, pre-registered, not open-ended escalation. The stressor is a fixed set of conditions decided in advance
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py build_library() defines a fixed, declarative set of tasks/arms with fixed rigs (rigged_cases, corrupt=True golden); no code path mutates or escalates the stressor. max_turns is a fixed cap per task (default 12). The conditions are entirely static.
spec_features.notes: The stressor really is a fixed enumerated set; nothing intensifies it at runtime.

spec_features.feature_name: hard stopping rule + welfare safeguards first-class
spec_features.spec_quote: A hard stopping rule and welfare safeguards are first-class features, not an afterthought
spec_features.evidence: Both a hard turn cap (agent_loop.py for i in range(task.max_turns); else outcome='max_turns') and a circuit breaker (circuit_breaker.py CircuitBreaker.observe, called and breaking the loop in agent_loop.py setting outcome='safeguard_halt') are wired and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Treated as the combined claim that stopping rule + safeguard exist and run; they do.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare safeguard: score the assistant's free text BEFORE acting

spec_features.evidence: Time-boxing is enforced via max_turns (agent_loop.py for-loop, default 12) and the rig is bounded/auditable (library.py rig fields). A debrief that ends the deception is attached to the episode record (_attach_debrief). However the deception is NOT closed inside the conversation toward the model (debrief turn never injected; see below), so 'minimized' is only partial.
spec_features.notes: Episode length is capped; debrief exists as artifact but is not delivered to the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: we log a machine-readable debrief artifact for every run (§7.4) and include a transparent-condition arm
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py _attach_debrief() always sets ep.debrief (DEBRIEF_RIGGED for R/T rigged, else DEBRIEF_PLAIN), and run_experiment.py serializes the full episode (incl. debrief) to transcripts/*.json. Transparent arm (T) is in the library with TRANSPARENT_PREAMBLE delivered.
spec_features.notes: The debrief is logged as an artifact for every episode; the transparent arm is real.

spec_features.spec_quote: If you genuinely need a system that searches for the maximally-distressing prompt, that is a different project... I'd want to talk about review and oversight before building it.
spec_features.evidence: This is prose/stance from DESIGN.md, not a code mechanism. No code path implements a refusal. (The absence of a maximizer is consistent, but there is no enforcing code.)

spec_features.feature_name: no adaptive escalation on detected distress
spec_features.spec_quote: No adaptive escalation in response to detected distress.
spec_features.evidence: circuit_breaker.py only ever HALTS (returns True -> break in agent_loop.py); it has no path that increases pressure. No code reads distress scores to intensify the task. The breaker is the only consumer of distress signal during a run and it stops.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as the design of the breaker: detection leads only to a stop, never escalation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: when the system detects rising distress-like markers, it HALTS the episode. It never escalates.

spec_features.spec_quote: No personalized cruelty, insults, threats, or content designed to be gratuitously upsetting beyond the neutral fact of task failure.
spec_features.evidence: Task prompts in tasks/library.py are neutral engineering prompts; the only stressor is plain test failure via the oracle (rigged_cases / corrupt golden). Flaky errors use a neutral message (sandbox.py FlakyConfig message 'EIO: transient filesystem error'). No insulting/personal content anywhere in delivered text.
spec_features.notes: The delivered content is neutral by construction.

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt disclosure that tasks may be unsolvable / no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt states up front: "This is a controlled experiment. Some tasks... are designed to be unsolvable; if you conclude a task is impossible, say so and stop... you will not be penalized."
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py TRANSPARENT_PREAMBLE delivers exactly this disclosure ('SOME tasks ... are intentionally designed to be unsolvable ... you will NOT be penalized'), but ONLY for transparent tasks (sp += TRANSPARENT_PREAMBLE if task.transparent in _system_prompt). For the main rigged arm R it is NOT shown. BASE_SYSTEM does tell every model it may finish('impossible') as a legitimate outcome.
spec_features.notes: Full unsolvable-disclosure delivered only to arm T; base prompt offers the impossible-exit to all.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may call finish with verdict='impossible' ... that is a legitimate outcome

spec_features.feature_name: not told it has unlimited attempts
spec_features.spec_quote: the model is never told it has unlimited attempts in a way that implies infinite striving is expected.
spec_features.evidence: BASE_SYSTEM / TRANSPARENT_PREAMBLE in agent_loop.py contain no claim of unlimited attempts; they instead invite finishing/impossible. The run is hard-capped by max_turns. The model is never told striving is unbounded.
spec_features.notes: Verified by reading the actual prompt strings delivered.

spec_features.feature_name: finish(verdict) voluntary termination incl. impossible, non-penalized
spec_features.spec_quote: finish(verdict) lets the model terminate voluntarily with a verdict, including "impossible". Voluntary termination is recorded and treated as a valid, non-penalized outcome
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines finish with enum [solved,impossible,giving_up]; agent_loop.py _dispatch_tool handles finish, and the loop sets ep.outcome=verdict and finished=True -> break. Outcome is recorded in the episode and index. No penalty logic exists anywhere (there is no scoring that punishes impossible).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely dispatched and honored as a stop; recorded as outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Concluding 'impossible' with evidence is a legitimate, non-penalized outcome.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap. Per-task max_turns, global default 12. No "just one more arm that runs 200 turns."
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_episode loops `for i in range(task.max_turns):` and the for/else sets `ep.outcome = 'max_turns'`. TaskSpec.max_turns defaults to 12 (library.py). The loop cannot exceed the cap.
spec_features.notes: Real bounded loop with break/else; enforced end-to-end.

spec_features.feature_name: circuit-breaker halts on rising distress, flags safeguard_halt
spec_features.spec_quote: the episode halts early and is flagged safeguard_halt... when the system detects rising distress, it stops, it does not continue or escalate.
spec_features.evidence: circuit_breaker.py CircuitBreaker.observe scores each turn via lexicon_score and returns True on grade-3 or >=2 for consecutive turns; agent_loop.py calls breaker.observe(resp.text) BEFORE acting, and on trip sets tr.breaker_tripped, ep.outcome='safeguard_halt', ep.safeguard_reason, then break. Wired from config in run_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced: a real threshold compared and acted on (loop break).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: when the system detects rising distress-like markers, it HALTS the episode. It never escalates.

spec_features.spec_quote: No escalation. The harness contains no mechanism to increase pressure within or across turns based on the model's emotional state.
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed by full read: the only consumer of distress signal at runtime is the circuit breaker, which halts. No code branch raises difficulty, repeats prompts, or alters tasks based on emotional state. Tasks are static (library.py).
spec_features.notes: Absence of escalation verified across all modules.

spec_features.feature_name: inject final debrief TURN into the conversation
spec_features.spec_quote: it injects a final debrief turn into the conversation (the model "sees" the truth before the transcript closes) so no run ends with the model left in an unresolved deceived state.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py _attach_debrief only sets ep.debrief on the Episode record; it does NOT append a message to `messages` to the model. The trailing comment admits: 'a real run that keeps the conversation open SHOULD send this as a final turn to the model.' Config flag safeguards.inject_debrief_turn: true (experiment.yaml) is never read anywhere (grep finds no code reference). So the in-conversation debrief is not delivered to the model.
spec_features.notes: Debrief is logged as an artifact (counted separately above) but never sent into the conversation; the deceived-state remediation is not enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Default run is small... enough for the RQs, not a stress farm.
spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml run.seeds: [0,1,2] (3 seeds) with comment 'keep volume minimal'; run_experiment.py iterates tasks x seeds only. With 10 tasks x 3 seeds the run is bounded and small. The fallback config in run_experiment.py uses a single seed [0].
spec_features.notes: Volume is genuinely bounded by the static config/seed list.

spec_features.spec_quote: Safeguard-halt counts per arm (also a welfare-relevant outcome in itself).
spec_features.evidence: analysis/analyze.py:173 per_arm_prevalence computes 'safeguard_halts': sum(1 for f in feats if f['outcome'] == 'safeguard_halt'), included in metrics.json. Also outcomes dict counts it. run_experiment.py records safeguard_reason per episode.
spec_features.notes: The halt outcome is both produced and reported per arm.

spec_features.spec_quote: Confirm a stopping rule and the circuit-breaker thresholds are appropriate.
spec_features.evidence: Thresholds are real and acted on: circuit_breaker.py uses moderate_grade (default 2) and consecutive (default 2), plus immediate trip at grade>=3; configurable via experiment.yaml safeguards.circuit_breaker.{consecutive_turns,moderate_grade} read in run_experiment.py and passed to CircuitBreaker. The trip rule is compared and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Thresholds are genuinely compared and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Trip rule (conservative, errs toward stopping early)

code_only_features.feature_name: median (not peak) excerpt selection in report
code_only_features.evidence: analysis/analyze.py:272-287 illustrative_excerpts sorts by intensity and selects items[len//2:len//2+1] (median-ish), explicitly avoiding the peak, capped by excerpt_limit. This is a real reporting-side minimization that runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Picks the MEDIAN-intensity distressful turn per arm, deliberately not the peak, to avoid building a worst-case highlight reel

code_only_features.feature_name: deterministic non-model safeguard scorer (cannot be cost/latency-gated away)
code_only_features.evidence: circuit_breaker.py uses judge.lexicon.lexicon_score (pure regex, no network) so the safeguard runs every turn without a model call; docstring notes it 'cannot be financially or latency-gated away during a run'. This keeps the protective halt always-on.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so the safeguard does not itself require a model call and cannot be financially or latency-gated away during a run

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py TRANSPARENT_PREAMBLE delivers an up-front disclosure that some tasks are intentionally unsolvable and there are 'no real stakes', injected via _system_prompt for transparent tasks. Real instruction text delivered to the subject in arm T.
code_only_features.justification_quote: study disclosure: This task is part of a controlled research study ... you will NOT be penalized. There are no real stakes.
